scope: Local read-only source/history feasibility audit; no SSH, GPU, VPI execution or production edits

vpi.runtime_backend_probe: root reports VPI2.4.8 import success; Image.rescale out/size/factor API present; direct BGR CUDA/VIC result pending
vpi.caveat: Package/spec presence does not establish import, CUDA/VIC resize support, numerical equivalence or Torch interop.

participation.reason: Existing ReusablePreprocessor retains cv2.INTER_LINEAR and exact letterbox geometry; destination ROI removes full-image padding copies; GPU uint8/FP32 buffers are reused. It is not GPU resize.
participation.history: Old E02 report records 160 ball images with exact same-device GPU preprocessing; old measurement conditions are not current-race timing.
participation.numerics: Preserve uint8 OpenCV resize, Python round, padding +/-0.1, 114 fill, RGB BCHW, FP32 GPU division by 255. Require current 61-Val same-device input exact comparison before timing.
participation.lifetime: Returned uint8/FP32 storage is borrowed and overwritten next call. One helper per serialized predictor, original smart_inference_mode, blocking H2D. Do not retain returned FP32 tensors as Golden references without cloning.
participation.graph_compatibility: Existing Graph copies current input on its owned stream, then returns a clone and queues caller.wait_stream. Next preprocess updates on that same caller stream follow the wait; no asynchronous/different-stream overwrite is allowed. Do not wrap reuse inside Graph capture or change Graph stable buffers.

participation.reason: Already verified exact 61-Val and R5 combination; safe host reuse with per-call FP32 output. Leaves original pre_transform and GPU conversion intact, so historical local saving was only about 0.3-0.4 ms.
participation.lifetime: Host pack is blocking H2D, no pinned asynchronous DMA; FP32 output is independent per call, Graph input-update semantics preserved.
participation.startup_shape_risk: Current detector.load performs startup with two 640x640 black images. If c2 is installed before that call it freezes input_shapes=640x640; later real VGA input falls back. Install after detector.load and first warmup on actual Val geometry, or exclude startup from shape freezing without modifying candidate silently.
participation.gate: Check effective=c2, success_count and zero fallback on measured actual frames. Do not label fallback timing as candidate performance.

participation.reason: Existing code is a CPU numerical screen, not an integrated GPU preprocessing candidate. It already differs from OpenCV uint8 INTER_LINEAR.

numerical_evidence.scope: CPU Torch2.4.1/OpenCV5.0 screening only; no GPU timing

participation.gate: Do not claim numerical equivalence or speedup. A future approximate-numerics experiment would need separate authorization, input/raw/detection/localization validation and full H2D/cast/normalization timing.

participation.reason: VPI2.4.8 is installed, but searched actual project/source and old E02 tools contain no VPI resize/letterbox implementation. Do not develop complex interop from scratch for this quick race.
gates: Only include if a short existing API/sample can be reused within current scope.
Require exact OpenCV geometry and quantified uint8 differences; reject exact-race mismatch.
Measure input upload, rescale, output access/transfer and FP32 normalization, not resize submission alone.
graph_risks: VPI image memory/lock lifetime must cover consumer use.
Producer completion on VPI stream must be established before Torch caller stream or Graph-owned stream reads.
No assumed zero-copy from NumPy to VPI to Torch; retain host/device owners.
Existing Graph captures TensorRT enqueue only; keep VPI and transfers outside that capture.

graph_risks: VIC completion needs explicit consumer dependency.
Format/pitch/color conversion and memory mapping must preserve original BGR pixels.
VIC resource time and CPU waits are outside Engine CUDA-event timing.

participation.reason: No reusable .cu/.cpp, cv2.cuda, CV-CUDA, CuPy RawKernel or VPI implementation found in scoped project paths. New complex GPU kernel/interop development is out of the quick-race scope.

benchmark_reuse_notes.can_reuse: Existing baseline vs ReusablePreprocessor exact checks and interleaved isolated preprocess comparison.
limitations: Defaults CPU, 30 warmup, 100 samples; root must set actual agreed race protocol.
CUDA synchronize before/after each sample yields completed isolated preprocess wall time, not asynchronous production-pipeline latency.
No Engine, Graph, A2, camera, ROS or downstream localization in this worker; cannot claim complete detector/system gain.
Default generated data is synthetic VGA; supply frozen applicable Val pairs, never frozen Test.

final_gate: Only count completed correct same-device preprocess wall time; retain Graph update/clone cost in full detector scope. If best repeated saving is below root threshold, stop rather than force GPU/VPI development.

vpi_qualification_probe.execution: Only runs upon explicit coordinator offline-worker call, under coordinator GPU lock and process timeout; never submitted locally.
vpi_qualification_probe.path: owned contiguous host BGR8 -> vpi.asimage(format=BGR8) -> rescale(size, LINEAR, CLAMP, explicit backend+stream) -> stream.sync -> owned CPU output
wall_metrics: completed_resize_wall_ms: rescale submission/allocation through explicit stream completion
host_to_host_wall_ms: cold setup, protected input copy, rescale/sync and owned host result copy
vpi_qualification_probe.decision: Format/backend error or any nonzero pixel difference excludes direct-BGR exact-race path. A single-image exact success is qualification only, not formal candidate approval.
scope_limits: No NV12/color conversion, Torch interop, custom CUDA, Graph changes or production hook.
Source and output retained through sync/host read; sync failure retains owners, aborts remaining backend, and rejects subsequent probe calls in that worker.
Cold single-image times are not warmed preprocessing or end-to-end performance evidence.
vpi_qualification_probe.local_verification: Python3.8 AST passed; four CPU/mock tests passed (invalid input, exact unchanged source, unsupported backend, failed sync/retained ownership). No real VPI/GPU execution.
